title: Short Squeezes and Their Consequences
one_line: Short squeezes (lenders recalling shares) are rare except in high-utilization, high-fee stocks, where they cost short sellers 56-73 bp a month and eat more than two-thirds of the −1.29%/month return of those stocks.

findings.statement: At ≥ 90% utilization, a squeeze roughly every 11 days; at ≤ 25%, once in 40 years.
Squeeze costs 0.87-1.04%/month vs −1.29%/month excess return for high-utilization stocks.

why.pattern: Limits to arbitrage via recall risk.

reported_results.headline: Short squeezes (lenders recalling shares) are rare except in high-utilization, high-fee stocks, where they cost short sellers 56-73 bp a month and eat more than two-thirds of the −1.29%/month return of those stocks.

data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
